_why_user_and_not_service_account: MOS-DATA-021 resolves `clinical_viewer` from a `User` with `study.read` under a
Deployment whose clinical_use_mode is `clinical`, and that is the row whose
egress column reads 'De-identification on egress: none'. A service_account here
would resolve to `service`, which MUST be de-identified, and the Gateway would
correctly refuse every retrieval with 503 deid_not_implemented.
REPORTED: this principal is the VIEWER, not the person using it. A real
deployment authenticates the clinician (OIDC) and this row disappears; until
then every clinical_viewer audit row names `user:ohif-viewer` and the
per-patient access trail cannot say WHICH clinician looked.

_why_platform_writer: MOS-DATA-020: 'The platform DICOM writer (Chapter 4) is the only principal that
may STOW AI-derived objects, and it does so through the Gateway with a
`platform_writer` principal. It operates in the SOURCE UID space
(MOS-DATA-021), because the objects it writes must reference the study as the
hospital knows it.' medos-worker IS that writer: medos/medos/writer/{seg,sr}.py is
Chapter 4's writer and the worker is the process that runs it.
REPORTED AS A DEVIATION: the same process also RETRIEVES the source series, and
MOS-DATA-021 classes a retrieving ServiceAccount as `service`, which must be
de-identified. The weeks 1-2 worker is both the control-plane runner and the
capability host in one process, so it cannot be both classes at once, and the
source-UID-space half is the one that governs what it writes. When capabilities
move into real Service containers (Triton / sealed services), those containers
get their own `service` principals and de-identification stops being optional.
Until then this single override is where the gap is visible.
